requirement.statement: Workbench Flow Editor SHALL render both flow-level and node-level authoring from product-owned StructureSchema plus optional EditorPresentation through the canonical Schema Editor compiler, lowering, Session, and renderer lifecycle.

case.given: A supported Flow product exposes an authorable flow target or selected node target
case.when: The right configuration panel opens that target
case.then: The panel SHALL compile StructureSchema and optional EditorPresentation to EditorPlan, lower it to the canonical schemaEditor.Editor shell, and render it through the existing CanonicalHalfcodeRenderer

case.when: The active Workbench source and dependency graph are inspected
case.then: The hand-written NodeSchema field bundle, bespoke field commands, bespoke runtime/session, and direct field renderer SHALL NOT remain as an active or fallback path

requirement.statement: Workbench SHALL own Flow-specific schema annotations, EditorPresentation overlays, SchemaEditorDialect classifiers and transformers, and business presenter registries inside a capsule without leaking Flow concepts into the reusable dg-cell-mvi Schema Editor base.

case.given: The default dialect and ordered Workbench product dialects classify the same schema field
case.when: The compiler resolves the field presenter
case.then: The fixed base precedence and later scoped business layer SHALL select the product presentation without mutating another editor Scope

case.given: The Workbench schema-editor capsule dependency graph is inspected
case.then: Workbench SHALL use package-root Schema Editor APIs and reusable packages SHALL NOT import Workbench Flow modules or presenters

requirement.statement: Workbench SHALL expose typed recursive scalar, object, collection, map, union, and reference controls for normal Flow authoring and SHALL NOT use an implicit JSON textarea or raw/code presenter fallback.

case.given: A Flow field declares nested array, object, or map structure
case.when: The schema-only or presentation-overlay editor is rendered
case.then: The user SHALL discover recursive item or entry controls and standard insert, remove, edit, move, add, remove, or rename operations as applicable

case.given: A product intentionally requires advanced raw JSON or code editing
case.then: A raw/code control SHALL appear only when EditorPresentation explicitly selects its stable presenter id and unsupported implicit cases SHALL render diagnostics instead

requirement.statement: The Workbench Flow ValueHost SHALL translate one concrete SchemaEditorCommand into the existing Flow capsule mutation path and SchemaEditorSession SHALL advance only from current-revision accepted canonical persistence feedback.

case.given: A presenter event resolves to a valid SchemaEditorCommand for a captured flow or node target
case.when: The Session dispatches it to the Workbench ValueHost
case.then: The ValueHost SHALL delegate through the existing product capsule and SHALL NOT directly import or call an XNL or VFS writer

case.given: Validation, canonical reload, VFS persistence, revision, identity, stale response, or host execution fails
case.when: The ValueHost returns rejected or conflict feedback
case.then: The Session and rendered panel MUST retain the previous accepted snapshot and authoritative revision

requirement.statement: InstantFlow, WorkFlow, and BizProcess SHALL support typed If branch and Fallback strategy insertion, removal, field editing, and drag reordering while preserving matching child bodies and canonical CtrlFlow port order.

case.given: An If node has structured branches with id, when, and optional config
case.when: The user inserts, removes, edits, or drags a branch
case.then: The owning product adapter SHALL emit structural XnlMutation operations that preserve matching branch bodies and the committed branch order SHALL drive the reloaded right-side CtrlFlow ports

case.given: A Fallback node has ordered strategies
case.when: The user inserts, removes, edits, or drags a strategy
case.then: The owning product adapter SHALL preserve matching strategy bodies and persist the requested canonical order

requirement.statement: EagerDataFlow SHALL expose discoverable typed controls for inputs, outputs, waitFor, implementation references, flow references, and config while keeping derived fields non-authorable.

case.given: An EagerDataFlow node declares inputs, outputs, or waitFor
case.when: The user edits map entries or collection items
case.then: The editor SHALL preserve port names and typed flow-port or flow-node references and canonical reload SHALL reproduce the corresponding DAG ports and edges

case.given: An EagerDataFlow node declares type, src, impl, flow, or config fields
case.when: The user opens the schema editor
case.then: The fields SHALL use discoverable semantic controls or explicitly selected advanced presenters and derived outputs SHALL remain unavailable for mutation

requirement.statement: Each supported Flow product SHALL expose product-owned flow-level StructureSchema and optional EditorPresentation for canonical root facts that are authorable, using the same Session and ValueHost protocol as node config.

case.given: A loaded InstantFlow, WorkFlow, BizProcess, or EagerDataFlow has authorable root configuration
case.when: The user selects the flow-level configuration target and edits a field
case.then: The edit SHALL use the product root schema, canonical mutation path, accepted feedback, and reload projection without fabricating derived fields

requirement.statement: InstantFlow, WorkFlow, BizProcess, and EagerDataFlow schema-editor operations SHALL persist through the existing exact XnlMutation batch, dry-run, canonical validation, VFS commit, and browser reload lifecycle.

case.given: A valid flow-level or node-level schema-editor command produces an XnlMutation batch
case.when: The candidate is validated and persisted
case.then: The exact dry-run batch SHALL be committed without recomputation and the accepted snapshot SHALL come from canonical reprojection after VFS success

case.given: Typed and structural edits have been accepted in each of the four products
case.when: The browser reloads the VFS-backed workspace
case.then: The canonical loader SHALL report no errors and the panel, XNL, graph ports, and product projection SHALL reproduce the committed values and order

requirement.statement: Schema-editor target switching, config editing, rejection, acceptance, and reload SHALL NOT take ownership of or corrupt CtrlFlow or DAGFlow layout, viewport, selection, renderer family, edge, or position facts.

case.given: A CtrlFlow or DAGFlow canvas has stable layout and viewport facts
case.when: A non-topology config command is accepted, rejected, or reloaded
case.then: The family-specific layout and viewport projection MUST remain unchanged

case.given: CtrlFlow branch order or DAG dependency fields change through canonical semantic mutation
case.when: The owning capsule reprojects the committed graph
case.then: Only that product family's canonical topology MAY change and the other family SHALL NOT receive foreign controls or layout semantics

requirement.statement: The migration SHALL be verified with real browser interactions, seeded chaos, full mechanical checks, legacy-residue scans, documentation, and a fresh independent verification that does not repair implementation.

case.given: The four Flow products are loaded in an isolated browser workspace
case.when: Playwright edits visible flow/node controls, performs structural add/remove/edit/drag operations, and reloads
case.then: The test SHALL use real controls, observe no page or console errors, and assert canonical persistence rather than dispatching internal store commands

case.when: Seeded chaos and a fresh verifier run against the live repositories
case.then: Family invariants, accepted-only state, package boundaries, no implicit JSON fallback, no legacy runtime, unit tests, typecheck, build, strict Codument validation, and replay artifacts SHALL be independently checked
